ordering_note: Threshold VALUES unchanged since first commit. The declared_* stamps are self-reported and NOT verifiable: block_boundary_automation first appears in commit 8acbbcd (committed 2026-10-27T15:48:58Z, earlier than its 16:05Z stamp), and midstream_genuine_automation first appears in 243fa0b (committed 16:08:29Z) together with splice_validity.cpp and its output. Each thresholds.json change was committed together with its results (2f377e9, 8acbbcd, 243fa0b), so declaration-before-measurement cannot be proven from git. The splice criterion is a fixed 1e-6 equality used only to refuse claims.

metric_definitions.max_abs_error: max |candidate - reference| over all samples and channels

notes: Full-plugin fidelity claim per case only if BOTH criteria pass. Kernel unit tests (tests/deesser/test_processor.cpp) are separate and make no fidelity claim. Held-out inputs are not used for tuning.

block_boundary_automation.reason: Original oracle (runtime/oracle.py, RUNNER_CONTRACT.md) fixes controls before processing; no intra-render automation timeline exists, so no genuine automation comparison is possible. These thresholds apply to the Tsunami core only and make no fidelity claim.
block_boundary_automation.signal: 48 kHz mono, 0.5-amplitude sine at 7 kHz, 512-sample blocks, parameter changed between blocks

metrics.max_gain_step: Wideband mode: max |g[n]-g[n-1]| with g=y/x over samples |x|>=0.1, in the 2048 samples after the change
metrics.click_excess: max |y[n]-y[n-1]| after the change minus max |x[n]-x[n-1]| (input slew), Wideband and Split

pass_criteria.max_gain_step_basis: recovered fast attack smoother 0.5 ms one-pole at 48 kHz bounds each gain step to 1-exp(-1/24)=0.0408 of the remaining gap; 0.05 allows quantization slack

meter.gain_reduction_db_active: >= 3 dB after 4096 samples of the test tone at -40 dB threshold

midstream_genuine_automation.oracle_support: none: runtime/RUNNER_CONTRACT.md lines 13 and 44 ('Controls fixed before processing; sampled automation timeline not yet supported'; 'No intra-render automation timelines, persistent-instance chaining'); host.py sets every control once, then calls plugin(x, sr, buffer_size=block, reset=True) on a fresh instance
midstream_genuine_automation.splice_model: output = static render A for n<N, static render B for n>=N. Only a valid stand-in for a genuine mid-stream change if the processor state at N is independent of the changed parameter (otherwise B's state at N is the state of a run that always had B).
midstream_genuine_automation.splice_validity_test: measured on the Tsunami core only (genuine internals are not observable through the oracle): continuous run with change A->B at block boundary N vs splice of two static core runs on the same input
midstream_genuine_automation.signal: 48 kHz mono 0.5-amplitude 7 kHz sine, 1 s, 512-sample blocks, change at N=24064 (start of block 47)
midstream_genuine_automation.consequence: if invalid for a case, no genuine mid-stream comparison is made for it; if valid only on the Tsunami core, the genuine comparison still requires the unverifiable assumption that the original has no parameter smoothing, so it is NOT run as a parity claim
